rule: Pieces (4-connected non-background components on a red background) have blue bodies and marker cells coloured 3/4/8. Each marker colour that appears on exactly two pieces is a join. The two pieces are translated without rotation so that the matching markers become orthogonally adjacent, leaving each marker's own bounding-box side. The output is the bounding box of the assembled pieces, with background elsewhere. Lone marker colours stay on their piece.
scope: Background 2, body 1 and marker palette {3,4,8} are fixed, as in every demonstration. Random scenes have 2-4 pieces. Grids are 13x13 half the time; otherwise width and height are each sampled independently from 10..20, which is a synthetic size extension. Explicit width and height may be 9..30. Piece boxes are 2..8 per side, and pieces are blob or ring shapes that span their box. Join trees are mostly path-shaped; star-shaped trees are a synthetic extension. An optional lone-marker distractor is added when a colour is spare. Not supported: rotation or flipping of pieces, join markers on box corners, marker colours used more than twice, cyclic join graphs, and body or background colours other than 1 and 2.

known_limitations: The palette is fixed at background 2, body 1 and markers {3,4,8}, matching all fixtures. It is not recoloured.
At most three joins, because only three marker colours exist. So there are at most four pieces.
Star join trees and grid sizes other than 13x13 are synthetic extensions not shown in the demonstrations.
The fallback phase after 400 failed attempts produces plain 3x3 chained pieces. It is randomized but simpler than the main sampler.
Very small explicit grids (such as 9x9) with 4 pieces mostly rely on the fallback phase.
Bounded validation is not proof of complete task semantics.

authored_constraints: Input pieces are 4-connected, span their bounding boxes and are separated by at least one background cell, so they never touch.
Each join colour occurs on exactly two different pieces. Exactly one direction leaves both marker boxes in the required way, so the join direction is unambiguous.
Join markers are on non-corner side cells, and the partner marker is on the opposite side.
Assembled pieces never overlap, so the reference solver's greedy placement with an overlap check agrees with the latent placement.
The join graph is a tree spanning all pieces, so the assembly is the same from any start piece.
Background is a strict majority of input cells.
The output is at most 30x30. Early attempts keep it no larger than the input.
Input never equals output, because input pieces are separated while joined pieces are adjacent.
